text:
Evil Dead Burn Review
Evil Dead Burn continues more than 40 years of Deadites conjured from the Necronomicon and wreaking bloody, gruesome and sometimes funny havoc upon the world. For as straightforward a story as that is, it's still difficult to nail the spirit of Sam Raimi's original cult classic. Following a Fede Alvarez reboot and a Lee Cronin sequel, How well does Evil Dead Burn carry the franchise torch? IGN's Tom Jorgensen reviews the Sébastien Vaniček entry, chatting about its visceral, gore-splattered highs, the underbaked story-based lows and just how tricky a relationship The Evil Dead has always had with comedy.

Cancelling Your PS+ Subscription Won't Stop Sony From Killing Discs, Say Experts - IGN Daily Fix
In today's Daily Fix:
After Sony's bombshell anouncement that they would no longer release first-party titles on physical discs, many gamers took to the PlayStation Network webpage to unsubscribe from PlayStation Plus. But analysts say that even if hundreds of thousands of gamers unsubbed from PS Plus, it's a drop in the bucket to PlayStation's overall business model and would likely not persuade them to keep supporting physical media. In other gaming news, Bernie Sanders has taken aim at Xbox, posting on social media that the company's mass layoffs and hardware price troubles are more evidence that corporate tax breaks do nothing to create or even save jobs. And on a bittersweet note, Bungie offered a farewell gift for their Destiny 2 fans as a 'thank you' for years of support before formally ending major updates for the game.

Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Jason Momoa, Florence Pugh, Rebecca Ferguson, Isaach De Bankolé, with Charlotte Rampling, with Anya Taylor-Joy, and Robert Pattinson, and Javier Bardem, and features newcomers Nakoa-Wolf Momoa and Ida Brooke.

Now a ruthless Emperor, Paul must face the consequences of his reign as old allies return, terrifying new threats emerge, and betrayal lurks in every shadow. Haunted by visions of Imperial collapse and the reappearance of his long-lost love, Paul is drawn into a sweeping conspiracy, with Chani at the heart of its unfolding mystery. As rebellion brews and enemies close in, Paul must confront the true cost of power and the fate of those he loves the most.

Dune: Part Three opens in theaters on December 18, 2026.

author: IGN YouTube
text:
Echoes of Aincrad Review
Echoes of Aincrad reviewed by George Yang on PlayStation 5, also available on Xbox Series X/S and PC.

Sword Art Online games have mostly been decent, although never truly exceptional. Echoes of Aincrad is a half-step in the right direction with a novel story starring an original cast of characters without heavily relying on Kirito to help it stand out. However, the open zones and world design are big stumbles due to its restricted exploration, along with the lack of variety in both the environments and enemies. The fiery combat and the smithy’s hot iron coals don’t bring enough heat to thaw out the story’s glacial pacing, either. Echoes of Aincrad may seem like a hardcore Sword Art Online fan’s dream game, but divorced from the anime’s branding, it’s just a passable action-RPG.
